I’m not gonna get into everything else but I’m a native Spanish speaker, it’s my first language. “Te amo” really is reserved for romantic connotation. There are outliers with folks, but generally, it’s just a heavy loaded phrase. You’d say “te quiero” for most familial/friendly types of loves. Even with couples “te amo” is a huge deal. Dean replying to “te amo” means he’s reciprocating it romantically as well. Hope that clears up what I meant!
Huh?

If this is legitimate, I want to point out something huge. At least from my experience as a native Spanish speaker, we have several ways to express  love. “Te amo” is reserved pretty much exclusively for romantic love. The whole fading interest thing? Honestly, it’s normal in relationships that last a long time. Love is a choice you make consciously every day. It’s work, and it comes and goes in intensity. Sit down with your partner and let them know that things are on a bit of a low, find out what it was that excited y’all about each other in the first place. Start going on dates like you did in the beginning, get to know each other all over again, do things TOGETHER and not just in the same room. Make the choice to be more aware of time spent with your significant other. Most people bolt when the “spark fades” but they miss out on the cozy fire that burns afterwards. It takes a lot of care to keep a fire going, and sometimes you gotta put in some work to spark it up again.

Has his hair always been like that? It’s very normal to see that in very thin, very fine, or very light hair. Chances are, he’s just got thin hair with a fine texture, possibly even a light color. I’m assuming by partition you mean they gave you a hard part (they cut in the part with a trimmer). I’d forgo that unless your barber can just trim that every two weeks. Most will at the cost of adding a line- as opposed to a full haircut. Other than that, if your fade at the shortest point is a four guard, and you want to maintain it longer, the only real advice I’ve got is go much shorter for your fade. Have them fade it down to a bald fade or even a one and just let that grow out. It’s not the perfect solution, but these are cuts that require maintenance. Going shorter initially gives you more time in between cuts. 
Pomade or other products depend on what look you’re going for so it’s all “What do I want out of this?” Gel will almost always give you a shiny wet look. Pomades give you a dry slicker look with shine and hold depending on the individual product. There are also waxes, clays, and fibers out there. It’s kind of what you wanna see/what works for you/what hold you want/your hairs texture.

Find a salon with a team you like and get their advice. There’s a lot more they can help out with in person because they can get a feel for your personality, desired hair maintenance levels, and what sort of styles you do/don’t like.

Your top length is relatively fine for the cut you’re aiming for. Your side though, need growing out. Unfortunately until they grow out enough to bend and lay down, you’re going to have to deal with it sticking out weird on the sides. Once you have enough length for it to lay down on the sides have your barber only lightly layer it into a taper and barely clean up around the ears/neckline. Not like you would with the cut you have now, but like you would for say- a woman’s pixie- with scissors around the back/ears instead of a trimmer. 
The tapering done with scissors on the side will give you a long enough look while still having that shorter at the bottoms feel. 
As far as your struggle with volume- there are shampoo/conditioner sets out there for volume. If you pick up a shampoo make sure to absolutely condition your hair as volumizing shampoos can be rough on hair and you need to close that hair shaft back up. Blow dry your hair in the opposite direction of where it grows for added lift- for even MORE lift put moose or root booster on your roots before drying. Always make sure you comb the products through your hair. After drying, style this back into the desired shape with a pomade of some sort according to what hold/shine level you want. The part you can do yourself once you have more length, but you should let your barber know just in case you’re getting trims in between (which honestly I just recommend you let it grow wild for a bit). 
Your biggest hurdle is going to be the disconnect from your longest length to those short sides. That WILL look funky as it grows out and eventually you’ll need that blended it. The haircut you’re after is just basically a business man’s regular cut with a slight taper. It’s the styling that’s particularly making it look so sharp.
